newsitem.title: GREECE: DRACHMA FIRMS VS ECU, BONDS WEAK ON COST OF CARRY.
newsitem.headline: DRACHMA FIRMS VS ECU, BONDS WEAK ON COST OF CARRY.

text.p: The drachma was gaining ground against the ecu and the mark in late dealings and interbank depos eased in short periods but bonds were still suffering from the high cost of carry, dealers said.
"We have a trend reversal in ecu/drachma," said a chief forex dealer at a foreign bank."Ecu/drachma is trading around 309.79/84 in late trade from 310.10 at open."
The dealer added that ecu/drachma could dip further as some London-based players who went long ecu/drachma on Friday would be forced to take the loss and close out positions.
Ecu/drachma cruised above 310 shortly after Friday's fixing on mark buying from a large bank linked to a state utility.
Mark/drachma was softer, having fallen below 157 in late dealings.
Depos were easier in short-term tenors but the long-end of the curve was holding morning levels, dealers said.
High interbank rates were taking their toll on Greek bonds and FRNs with the discount margin on FRNs having risen to 102 basis points from 95 in early dealings, bond dealers said.

"Bonds and FRNs are suffering from the high cost of funding and some banks have opted to sell, even at a loss, expecting short-term rates to hold current levels or just ease in the near future," said a bond dealer.

Prices of 10-year bonds shed half a point to 94.50, seven-year bonds lost 35 basis points to 95.10, five-year taxable bonds 30 to 35 basis points to 97 and three-year taxable bonds due March 2000 shed 40 basis points to 98.10, dealers said.
"Bonds are going to recover from current levels provided that money rates ease," the dealer said. "Yields are undoubtedly very attractive and buying interest should pick up sooner or later."
The mark was quoted at 156.95/00 from Monday's 156.970 fix, the dollar at 281.55/65 drachmas from 282.000 and the ecu at 309.72/82 from 309.80 drachmas.
